_about: Further reading found for a concept or an algorithm: write-ups, tutorials, talks, posts. Attached to the concept and algorithm layers only -- the 841 entries are inherited from the source HTML and are not where this project's own work lives.
_not_sources: These are not sources. A source in this catalogue is a page that settled a specific question, and `sources.json` says so in its own rule: no link into a layer, no reason to be there. Further reading answers no question -- it is worth reading. Putting the two in one table would mean the sources page could no longer be read as 'every URL here was used to check something', which is the only thing that makes it worth having.
_verification: Every URL is fetched before it is accepted. A 200 is necessary and not sufficient: the returned title has to match what the model claimed, because a live URL that is not the page described is the same failure as a dead one. This is the rule `implementations.json` already applies to packages -- PyPI `sdf`, `wfc`, `pymo` and `meep` all returned 200 for something unrelated -- pointed at links instead.
_why_keep_rejects: A rejected candidate stays as a row with `rejected: true` and a reason. Two of the three models cannot browse at all, so they answer from memory, and the share of URLs they propose that turn out not to exist measures how much each one invents. That number is the whole argument for asking three models rather than trusting one, so discarding the failures would discard the evidence for the design.

_reasons.gone: 404, or the host no longer resolves.
_reasons.title-mismatch: The page loads and is not what it was described as.
_reasons.unreachable: Blocked, timed out, or refused from CI. Not proof the page is bad -- proof it cannot be checked from here.
